trigger: the Gear tab's BAG list when no carried item takes a slot
why: A fresh hero starts with an empty bag, so "nothing left" claimed a history the player never had; the heading now just states the fact.

trigger: the Gear tab's BAG list when no carried item takes a slot
before: You used it all. That was the plan, technically.
after: Nothing here takes a slot. Plenty of room for regret.
why: "You used it all" was wrong on turn one (and after a drop or a sale); the line now says what the empty state means, then the joke.

trigger: the Gear tab's HEALING POTION row in CONSUMABLES
after: Heals 7–25 hp (double for a Wilmsry). Stays corked at full health.
why: The row gave no amount, and the row is disabled at full health, so a potion is never wasted there; it now names drinkPotion's 7–25 hp, the Wilmsry double, and the refusal.

trigger: the Gear tab's WORN weapon row note for an enchanted weapon
after: +{n} damage, and it hits what only magic can. Somebody cared, once.
why: "+N magic" never said what the enchantment does; the engine adds it to damage and lets the weapon touch magic-only foes.

trigger: the Gear sheet's USE line for a recharging charged item
after: {k} of {max} charges left; the next one comes back in {n} squares.
why: The sentence repeated the row tag ("Charges 1/3 · 5 SQ."); it now says how many charges are left and when the next one returns (one per recharge).

trigger: the Gear sheet's USE line for a recharging charged item
after: {k} of {max} charges left; the next one comes back in 1 square.
why: The singular form of the new recharge sentence, so one square does not read "1 squares".

trigger: a staff's stat line (Gear sheet, store row)
before: Wielded: {lab} weapon; its power works only in hand.
after: Fights as a {lab} weapon; its power works only while wielded.
why: "Wielded: d8 weapon" read like a label that the staff was already in hand, even on a bagged staff; the line now says how it fights and when its power works.

trigger: why a store or loot item is, or is not, an upgrade
why: The numbers had no unit; they are expectedStrike's average damage per swing, misses and crits included.

trigger: why a store or loot item is, or is not, an upgrade
why: "Practiced bonus" never said what it adds; the proficiency the swap resets is a flat damage term.

trigger: the Hero tab's Abilities list for a Magic User
after: No abilities. Spells are the trick.
why: The joke stood in for the fact; the empty state now says there are no abilities first, then the joke.

trigger: the Hero tab's Special skills heading (a Fighter's or Thief's chargen skill budget)
why: "12/12 vp" named a unit the game never explains; it is how many of the class's chargen skill points the rolled skills used.

trigger: a found or looted bag's compare line
why: "12 slots — you carry 8" read as eight items carried; the number is the current bag's slot count, so the clause is now chosen per case (below).

trigger: a found or looted bag's compare line
why: The current bag's capacity now reads "yours holds 8", so the comparison is slots against slots.

trigger: a found or looted bag's compare line
why: The bag-less case keeps its words; "you carry" moved into the literal because the clause is now chosen whole.

before: · triple for armour, double for arms
why: Nothing in the engine sets a store markup, so the clause could never show, and it described a rule the game does not have (prices vary by race, via priceFor).

trigger: the store screen's header and sections
before: A store … wilmst in your purse… … … Your gear Leave
after: A store … wilmst in your purse … … Your gear Leave
why: The purse line lost the dead markup interpolation above; its words are unchanged.
